verdict: The family classification STANDS, now with the precise mechanism and rates: oauth_callback reds are a SAME-BINARY port-space race inside pa-core's mcp::oauth_callback tests - the sibling test all_candidates_bound_fails_clearly binds the full 10-port callback range 53700-53709 by design and holds it for its duration, so any same-binary test that concurrently calls CallbackServer::start().await.unwrap() panics on the product's DESIGNED error 'Could not start the OAuth callback server: ports 53700-53709 are all in use'. 3 direct unguarded victims (callback_flow_settles_code_and_state, error_callback_settles_none, unknown_route_is_404_without_settling) + falls_back_to_the_next_free_port as a transient-window victim (its own base-port blocker is guarded, but the sibling's mid-pass can hold the other 9 ports while it starts). Rates per dispatch context at tip a5235b123: SOLO 0/10 (5/5 release + 5/5 debug green, the member that reds), family-filter default-threads 14/20 debug (70%) + 4/10 release (40%), --test-threads=1 0/5 (the mechanism proof - sequential dispatch cannot co-schedule), full-suite co-scheduled x2 module 6/6 GREEN both runs (0 collision messages), CI 0/1531 runs (zero module failures, zero collision messages), pooled-VM era 1/109 module-run logs. Combined full-suite co-scheduled fleet rate 2/113 ~ 1.8% (pool era 1/109 + mcplogin-triage 1/2 + this lane 0/2). NOT environmental (the listener binds 127.0.0.1 numeric - no DNS leg, unlike mcp_login); NOT a code red; cargo runs test binaries sequentially so cross-binary collision is impossible - the family needs the module's own tests co-scheduled in one binary. Registration RENEWED (expiry 2026-10-01) with mechanism + rates + remedy design + reopen trigger; auto-citation verified.

mechanism.the_range_holder: all_candidates_bound_fails_clearly (crates/pa-core/src/mcp/oauth_callback.rs #[cfg(test)]): binds ALL 10 candidate ports 53700..53709 with a std::net::TcpListener::bind loop (filter_map over (0..CALLBACK_PORT_COUNT)), asserts the designed all-busy error, and holds every listener until test end - the full range is occupied for its whole duration.
mechanism.the_victims: callback_flow_settles_code_and_state, error_callback_settles_none, unknown_route_is_404_without_settling - each runs CallbackServer::start('Linear').await.unwrap(); start() scans the 10-port range and returns Err('Could not start the OAuth callback server: ports 53700-53709 are all in use. ...') when the sibling holds the range; the unwrap panics -> test FAILED. falls_back_to_the_next_free_port holds the BASE port as its own blocker (guarded: skips when the base is already held) but also unwraps start() - it is a victim only through the sibling's TRANSIENT mid-pass window (the sibling grabs the other 9 ports during its filter_map pass while the base is blocked, so start() sees all 10 busy). query_and_percent_decoding binds no port (pure string fns) and never reds; the range holder itself never reds (it asserts the error).
mechanism.why_same_binary_only: cargo executes test binaries one at a time and the CI shard script runs each test unit as its own cargo invocation, so only tests inside the SAME pa-core lib binary can overlap the range; the harness's default thread pool = vCPU count, which sets the collision probability (8c VM family-filter 70% debug; fewer/scattered dispatch = the full-suite ~1.8% and the 4-vCPU CI 0/1531).
mechanism.failure_signature: panicked at .unwrap() on CallbackServer::start with 'Could not start the OAuth callback server: ports 53700-53709 are all in use. Close other login attempts and retry.' - one line per victim; every observed red of this family carries it (14/14 red family-filter runs, the pooled-era review red, the mcplogin run1 red); zero reds without it.
